title: Longest Common Prefix
description:
# Longest Common Prefix

Given an array of lowercase strings `strs`, return the longest string that is a prefix of every string in the array.

A prefix starts at the first character of a string and may be the whole string. If the strings do not share any first character, return the empty string `""`.

## Example 1:

**Input:** strs = ["flower","flow","flight"]
**Output:** "fl"
**Explanation:** All three strings start with `"fl"`, but `"flo"` is not a prefix of `"flight"`.

## Example 2:

**Input:** strs = ["dog","racecar","car"]
**Output:** ""
**Explanation:** The first characters already differ, so there is no common prefix.

## Constraints:

* `1 <= strs.length <= 200`
* `0 <= strs[i].length <= 200`
* `strs[i]` consists of only lowercase English letters.
* An empty string inside the array makes the answer `""`.

solutions.name: Horizontal Prefix Shrinking
solutions.timeComplexity: O(S) where S is the total number of characters
solutions.description:
## Approach

Keep a current candidate prefix, starting with the first string. For each later string, repeatedly remove the last character from the candidate until that string starts with it. Stop early if the candidate becomes empty.

## Key Insight

After processing the first `k` strings, the candidate is exactly their longest common prefix. The next string can only make that prefix shorter, never longer, so shrinking preserves the invariant.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(S), where `S` is the total number of characters inspected across the input strings.
- Space Complexity: O(1), ignoring the returned prefix string.

solutions.name: Vertical Character Scan
solutions.timeComplexity: O(S) where S is the total number of characters
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use the first string as a reference and scan character position by character position. At each position, compare the reference character with the same position in every other string. The first mismatch or shorter string gives the answer length.

## Key Insight

A common prefix is decided column by column. Once any string disagrees at position `i`, no longer prefix can be valid, and the first `i` characters are already known to be shared.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(S), with early stopping when the prefix ends.
- Space Complexity: O(1), ignoring the returned prefix string.

solutions.name: Divide and Conquer Merge
solutions.timeComplexity: O(S) where S is the total number of characters
solutions.description:
## Approach

Recursively split the array into halves. Compute the longest common prefix of the left half and the right half, then merge those two prefix strings by comparing them from the start.

## Key Insight

The longest common prefix operation is associative: the prefix shared by the whole array is the common prefix of the prefix from each half. That turns the problem into a clean reduction over subarrays.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(S), because each merge compares only prefix characters and the total useful comparison work is bounded by the input size.
- Space Complexity: O(log n) for the recursion stack.

solutions.name: Binary Search on Prefix Length
solutions.timeComplexity: O(S log m) where m is the shortest string length
solutions.description:
## Approach

First find the shortest string length. Binary search the answer length from `0` to that minimum length. For a candidate length, take that prefix from the first string and check whether every string starts with it.

## Key Insight

Prefix validity is monotonic by length. If all strings share a prefix of length `L`, then every shorter length is also valid. If length `L` fails, every longer length must fail.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(S log m), where `m` is the shortest input length.
- Space Complexity: O(1), ignoring temporary substring objects and the returned prefix string.

solutions.name: Trie Single-Branch Walk
solutions.timeComplexity: O(S) where S is the total number of characters
solutions.description:
## Approach

Insert every word into a trie. Starting from the root, keep walking while the current trie node has exactly one child and is not the end of a word. The characters along that single path form the common prefix.

## Key Insight

All strings share a prefix exactly while their trie paths are forced to use the same next edge. A branch means two strings differ; a terminal node means one string has ended and the prefix cannot extend further.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(S), where `S` is the total number of inserted characters.
- Space Complexity: O(S) for the trie nodes.
